Rwanda is a republic in Central Africa bordering Uganda to the north, Tanzania to the east, Burundi to the south, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

1000093.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Rwanda-Rundi u Rwanda (“Rwanda”), from the archaic Rwanda-Rundi verb -anda (“to expand”).
Compare Zulu -anda (“to increase, multiply; spread”). Parallel international forms include Norwegian Nynorsk Rwanda, Danish Rwanda, Swedish Rwanda, Dutch Rwanda and English Rwanda.

en.g: An inflectional suffix forming the indefinite neuter singular of many adjectives
Forming neuter singular forms of certain determiners, possessives, pronouns and numerals
Forming adverbs from adjectives, especially adverbs of manner, degree or viewpoint
Forming the supine of certain strong and irregular verbs, generally together with a change in the verbal stem
Forming the corresponding basic or neuter form of the past participle
x: The book was taken from the table.

1000349.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse -t (“neuter adjective and adverbial ending”). The adverbial use developed from the use of a neuter singular adjective form without an expressed noun. The Norwegian supine is likewise formally identical to the neuter singular of the past participle.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk -t, Danish -t, Swedish -t, Icelandic -t and Faroese -t (“neuter adjective and adverbial ending”).

Den demokratiske republikken Kongo (forkortet DR Kongo) er et land i Afrika
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (abbreviated DR Congo) is a country in Africa.

1000605.etyen:
First attested before 1999. Calque of French République démocratique du Congo (“Democratic Republic of the Congo”), the country's official French name. The corresponding state name was used from 1964 until 1971 and was restored in 1997 after the country had been known as Zaïre (“Zaire”). For the further origin of Kongo, see that entry.
Parallel calques include Norwegian Nynorsk Den demokratiske republikken Kongo, Danish Den Demokratiske Republik Congo, Swedish Demokratiska republiken Kongo, German Demokratische Republik Kongo, Dutch Democratische Republiek Congo and English Democratic Republic

en.g: Forming adjectives from nouns, indicating that something is provided or covered with, full of, characterized by, associated with, resembling, or belonging to what the noun denotes
Forming adjectives from verbs, with meanings resembling a present participle or indicating a characteristic, repeated or habitual action or manner

1001373.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse -aðr (“having, possessing”) and -óttr (“provided with, characterized by”), two adjective-forming suffixes which merged in Norwegian. The former ultimately derives from Proto-Germanic *-ōdaz, and the latter from Proto-Germanic *-uhtaz.
Compare Danish -et and Swedish -ad; related formations include older Swedish -ot, German -icht and Old English -eht (“adjective-forming suffix”).

en.g: a female given name from Norwegian

1004701.etyen:
Short form of Otilie, one of several Norwegian spellings of a female given name going back to Latin Otilia, originally Odilia, a Latinised form of Old High German Odila and Otila, pet forms of names such as Oda. The Old High German names are formed from the Germanic name element reflected in *audaz (“wealth, riches”), with a pet-name or diminutive ending.
Compare Danish Tilje, Swedish Tilje and English Tilly (“female given name”).
